lessons.title: What you own
lessons.keyIdea: The book lists what you already hold: stock, fund, cash, or crypto. An empty book is fine.
paragraphs: The Invest book is a list of what you already hold. A stock is a slice of one company. A fund is a basket of many names. Cash is money sitting as cash. Crypto is a coin the book can list.
The book does not buy or sell for you. You add a name when you own it. If the book is empty, that is fine — search still works. This page will not invent a position.
Type is a label so you can sort. Weight is how big that name is on the page. Missing price cache prints Unknown. The book is the source.

lessons.title: You can lose money
lessons.keyIdea: A price can fall. A green number is history, not a promise.
paragraphs: A price can fall. A name can go to zero. Profit and loss on the book is history, not a promise. You can lose money.
This app is educational. It is not financial advice. A green number today can be red later. Do not treat a chart or a score as a guarantee.
If you do not have holdings yet, you can still read this and search. Nothing here invents a position or a return. The book only shows what you add.

cta.label: Open Invest and read the book as it is

lessons.title: Don't put everything on one name
lessons.keyIdea: If one name is most of the book, a drop in that name hits the whole book. The bar shows your mix — not a sample.
paragraphs: Concentration means one name is a large share of the book. If that name drops, the whole book drops with it. Spreading across names is one way to reduce that single-name hit.
The book can show a concentration bar when you have holdings. This lesson will not invent weights. If the book is empty, there is nothing to concentrate yet.
There is no “right” mix on this page. The tool shows what you own. Use that, not a sample book from a lesson.

cta.label: Open the book and check mix

lessons.title: The book: quantity, average cost, profit/loss
lessons.keyIdea: Quantity, average cost, and P/L are book columns. Average cost is what you paid, not today’s price.
paragraphs: Quantity is how many units you hold. Average cost is what you paid per unit, on average. Profit or loss is today’s value versus what you paid — when a price is known.
Average cost is not today’s price and not a target. If a price is missing, the book can print Unknown. The book does not invent a gain.
Add a name only when you own it. Search is for looking up a public name. The columns on the book are the source of truth.

lessons.title: How to read a company page without drowning
lessons.keyIdea: Search a name you already know. Missing data prints Unknown. Do not fill gaps with a guess.
paragraphs: Search a name or ticker you already know. The company page is a read: price, facts, and a score when the cache has them. It is not a buy or sell ticket.
You do not need every box. Start with what it is, what it costs today, and whether the cache is fresh. Missing data prints Unknown. Do not fill gaps with a guess.
This lesson will not name a sample ticker. Type a public name you care about on Invest. You will land on a company page for that lookup — not a fake name from a lesson.

lessons.title: Options are advanced — skip until you want them
lessons.keyIdea: Options can expire worthless. The book and search work without them. Skip them for now.
paragraphs: Options are contracts about a price in the future. They can expire worthless. They are easy to misuse. You can skip them.
Invest still works without options. The book, search, and mix do not require them. If you are learning, stay on those.
When you want options later, they live under Invest. This slice does not lock the book. Both Learn and Do stay open.
